parts.text:
8
A ship of mass 8.4 × 107
kg is approaching a harbour with speed 16.4 m s–1. By using reverse
thrust it can maintain a constant total stopping force of 920 000 N.
How long will it take to stop?
A
15 seconds
B
150 seconds
C
25 minutes
D
250 minutes

hints: Notice the initial momentum from mass $8.4 \times 10^7 \text{ kg}$ and speed $16.4 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, and the constant stopping force of $920000 \text{ N}$.
Recall that stopping needs impulse $F \times t$ equal to change in momentum $m \times \Delta v$, so $t = mv/F$.
Calculate $t$ in seconds first, then divide by $60$ to compare with the options given in seconds and minutes.
walkthrough: Identify the change in momentum needed to stop: $\Delta p = m \Delta v = (8.4 \times 10^7) \times 16.4$.
State the impulse rule: constant force $F$ acting for time $t$ gives $F t = \Delta p$, so $t = m \Delta v / F$.
Calculate numerator: $8.4 \times 10^7 \times 16.4 = 1.3776 \times 10^9 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, then $t = 1.3776 \times 10^9 / 9.2 \times 10^5 \approx 1497 \text{ s}$.
Convert seconds to minutes: $1497 / 60 \approx 25$ minutes, with deceleration $a = F/m \approx 0.011 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ confirming a very slow stop.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 100. It ignores the large mass of $8.4 \times 10^7 \text{ kg}$ relative to the $920000 \text{ N}$ force.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10. The stopping time is about $1500 \text{ s}$, not $150 \text{ s}$.

C.explanation: Initial momentum $mv$ divided by $920000 \text{ N}$ gives about $1500 \text{ s}$, which is $25$ minutes.

D.explanation: Too large by a factor of 10. It corresponds to about $15000 \text{ s}$ rather than the calculated $1500 \text{ s}$.
